nodes.name: Microwave-polyol synthesis
nodes.procedure: HEA-QDs were synthesized through the microwave-polyol method at 230 °C for 80 s. The microwave thermal radiation rapidly decomposes the acetylacetone salts, forming seeds, and induces explosive nucleation and uniform growth in triethylene glycol (TEG). Meanwhile, TEG as a protecting agent can directly bind to the HEA surface preventing uncontrollable enlargement, thus stabilizing the HEA-QDs.
nodes.source_text: HEA-QDs were synthesized through the microwave-polyol method at 230 °C for 80 s as illustrated in Fig. 1b.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms high entropy atomic structure with uniform elemental distribution and average diameter of ca. 1.9 nm for ultra-small HEA-QDs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images display that the obtained HEA-QDs are uniformly dispersed with an average diameter of ca. 1.9 nm (Fig. 1c and d and Fig. S1, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD pattern displays broad peaks around 42.0° owing to ultra-small particle size and lattice distortion resulting from multiple elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1e, the powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern of HEA-QDs displays broad peaks around 42.0°, owing to the ultra-small particle size and lattice distortion resulting from multiple elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows various intensities of bright spots elucidating multielement composition with random distribution of multiple metallic elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To probe the atomic structural details of HEA-QDs, aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM was performed. As shown in Fig. 1f and Fig. S3 (ESI†), the various intensities of bright spots elucidate the multielement composition within HEA-QDs due to the different atomic number contrast.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows atomic ratio of Pt:Ru:Mo:Fe:Co:Ni as 17.3:17.0:17.4:16.0:5.9:8.1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) spectra show that the atomic ratio of Pt, Ru, Mo, Fe, Co, and Ni is 17.3:17.0:17.4:16.0:5.9:8.1.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDS and elemental maps display homogeneous distribution of Pt, Ru, Mo, Fe, Co, and Ni elements in single HEA-QDs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental maps (Fig. 1i) display the homogeneous distribution of elements Pt, Ru, Mo, Fe, Co and Ni in single HEA-QDs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge white line intensity significantly decreases and Ru K-edge absorption edge shifts left indicating excess electrons transferred to Pt (+0.94) and Ru (+0.3) valence bands compared to Pt/C and Ru/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with commercial Pt/C and Ru/C, the white line (WL) intensity of the Pt L3-edge significantly decreases (Fig. 2a) and the absorption edge of the Ru K-edge obviously shifts to the left (Fig. 2d) for HEA-QDs, which indicate that excess electrons are transferred into the valence band of Pt and Ru atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f peaks negatively shift by 0.6 eV and Ru 3p by 0.5 eV compared to Pt/C and Ru/C, suggesting electrons transferred from adjacent transition metal species to Pt and Ru sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to commercial Pt/C and Ru/C, the peaks in the Pt 4f and Ru 3p XPS spectra of HEA-QDs negatively shift by 0.6 and 0.5 eV, respectively (Fig. 2g and h), suggesting that electrons might be transferred from adjacent transition metal species to Pt and Ru sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band spectra show d-band center of HEA-QDs/C shifts down to -3.96 eV compared to Pt/C (-3.85 eV), Ru/C (-3.91 eV), and PtRu/C (-3.93 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to the values of Pt/C (-3.85 eV), Ru/C (-3.91 eV), and PtRu/C (-3.93 eV), the d-band center of HEA-QDs/C shifts down to -3.96 eV (Fig. 2i, top).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows average Pt–M bond length 2.1 Å and Ru–M 2.2 Å, significantly shorter than bulk Pt (2.6 Å) and Ru (2.4 Å); Pt–O at 1.7 Å and Ru–O at 1.5 Å also detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2c and f, the average bond lengths of Pt–M (2.1 Å) and Ru–M (2.2 Å) in HEA-QDs significantly differ from the metallic bond lengths in bulk Pt (2.6 Å) and Ru (2.4 Å) references.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS mapping confirms uniform elemental distribution of Pt, Ru, Mo, Fe, Co, Ni across HEA-QDs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental maps (Fig. 1i) display the homogeneous distribution of elements Pt, Ru, Mo, Fe, Co and Ni in single HEA-QDs.
